name: Paidcheck – Find Orders Paid with Stripe but Stuck in Pending for WooCommerce
author: mykytadudariev

sections.description:
Sometimes a customer pays with Stripe, but the WooCommerce order never hears about it: a webhook is missed, the customer closes the tab before the redirect back, or a confirmation gets lost. The money is in your Stripe account, while the order sits in “Pending payment”, “Failed”, “On hold” or even “Cancelled”, and the customer waits for goods that never ship.

Paidcheck finds those orders. Open WooCommerce > Paidcheck, choose how far back to look (1, 2 or 7 days) and press Check orders. Paidcheck reads each recent unpaid Stripe order’s payment from Stripe and sorts the results:

  • Paid, order not updated: Stripe has the full payment (or an uncaptured authorization on a pending or failed order), the order does not.
  • Paid, amount differs: Stripe has a payment, but for a different amount or currency.
  • No link to a Stripe payment: the order has no Stripe payment recorded, or Stripe does not know it.
  • Payment in progress: the payment is still processing or waits for the customer.
  • Could not check: Stripe could not be reached for that order; the reason is shown.

Each finding shows the order with a link to edit it, both amounts, both statuses, the payment time and the Stripe payment ID linked to your Stripe Dashboard, so you can fix the order by hand.

Read-only. Paidcheck never changes an order, never adds an order note and never creates, changes or cancels anything in Stripe. Orders created in the last 15 minutes are skipped, so payments still being confirmed are not reported.

Supported gateway. Paidcheck works with the official WooCommerce Stripe Gateway plugin, including its card, wallet and local payment methods. WooPayments is not supported: it does not give the store a Stripe key to read with. Other Stripe plugins are not supported either.

Where the Stripe key comes from. You choose on WooCommerce > Paidcheck > Settings. By default nothing is configured: Paidcheck uses the secret key that the WooCommerce Stripe Gateway has saved for its current mode (the test key in test mode, the live key otherwise), and does not store, display or log it. Optionally you can save your own restricted key with read access only, one for test mode and one for live mode, so that Stripe itself enforces that Paidcheck cannot change anything. A restricted key is stored in your site’s database, as the gateway stores its own keys, and is never shown again after you save it. When a restricted key is chosen, the gateway’s key is never used. The key is used only for the requests below.

The last result stays on the screen until the next check and holds order numbers, statuses, amounts and Stripe payment IDs only, no customer names, emails or addresses. Paidcheck supports High-Performance Order Storage.

External services

Paidcheck connects to the Stripe API (api.stripe.com), provided by Stripe, to read the payment state of your orders.

  • When: while a shop manager runs a check on the WooCommerce > Paidcheck screen, and once when a shop manager saves a restricted key for the gateway’s current mode, to confirm that it sees this store’s payments. Nothing is sent in the background.
  • What is sent: for each checked order, a read request for the PaymentIntent or Checkout Session ID that the WooCommerce Stripe Gateway recorded on the order, authenticated with the key you chose (the gateway’s secret key or your restricted key). When a restricted key is saved, up to three such read requests for the most recent orders’ PaymentIntents and one for the most recent order that recorded only a Checkout Session. No customer data is sent.
  • What is received: Stripe returns the full payment object, which includes the latest charge and, for a Checkout Session, the session. These can contain the customer’s billing name, email and address as Stripe recorded them. Paidcheck uses only the payment’s ID, status, amount, currency, creation time and refund flag; it stores and shows nothing else, and keeps no customer details.

Stripe Services Agreement and Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce and the WooCommerce Stripe Gateway.
  2. Install Paidcheck through the Plugins screen, or upload it to /wp-content/plugins/, and activate it.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Paidcheck and press Check orders.
sections.faq:
Will Paidcheck mark my orders as paid?

No. It only reports. Open the order from the report, compare it with the payment in your Stripe Dashboard and update it yourself.

Which orders are checked?

Orders placed with the WooCommerce Stripe Gateway in the last 1, 2 or 7 days that are pending payment, failed, on hold or cancelled, and older than 15 minutes.

The report says “No link” for an order that was paid. Why?

The order has no Stripe payment ID, or Stripe does not know that ID for the key in use. A common cause is an order paid in test mode while the gateway is now in live mode, or the other way round. The report shows which mode was checked.

Can I use a restricted key?

Yes, and it is the safer choice: a restricted key can only do what you allow. In the Stripe Dashboard open Developers > API keys > Create secret key, choose “Sharing with a third-party service” (vendor name Paidcheck), then “Custom permissions”. Set Payment Intents and Checkout Sessions to Read and leave every other permission on None. The key Stripe creates starts with rk_. Then open WooCommerce > Paidcheck > Settings, click “Use a read-only restricted key instead”, paste the key for the gateway’s current mode (live or test) and click “Save and verify”. Going back to the gateway’s key later removes the saved restricted keys. Paidcheck checks the key against a recent order’s payment before keeping it, and refuses a full secret key (sk_), a key for the other mode, a key without the needed permissions and a key that does not see this store’s payments, which most likely belongs to another Stripe account.

Who can use it?

Users who can manage WooCommerce, such as administrators and shop managers.

Does it work with many orders?

Yes. The check runs in small batches with a progress indicator, so hundreds of orders finish without hitting your server’s time limit.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Deleting Paidcheck removes its last result, any unfinished check and the restricted keys saved in its settings. Orders and gateway settings are never touched.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: save your own restricted Stripe key with read access only, instead of using the WooCommerce Stripe Gateway’s secret key. The key is checked against a recent payment when you save it.
  • WooCommerce > Paidcheck now has two tabs: Check orders and Settings.
  • The screen and each result now say which key was used. A scan with a restricted key that finds none of your payments warns that the key may belong to another Stripe account.
  • A line about Paidcheck Pro, in development, below results that have orders needing action.
  • Fix: on narrower screens the order and Stripe status badges in the report wrap instead of cutting the status short, as in “Pending paym…”.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

short_description: Find WooCommerce orders that Stripe says were paid but are still pending, failed, on hold or cancelled in your store.
